after: MngA is one 658-residue EIIABC chain. MC4100 mngA deletion loses MG transport and pACS31 restores it; inverted membranes plus general PTS extracts and PEP form MG-P. This is not a purified three-protein reconstitution. Separate intact-cell uptake comparisons in MG-induced MC4100 reported weak reduction with glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect with trehalose, and no observed reduction with fructose, maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol. The Discussion instead describes mannose and those three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar radiolabeled MG; the mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension remains unresolved. These are uptake comparisons, not direct binding, a proven competitive mechanism or inhibition constants. Separately, 300 mM NaCl during growth did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%; this is an induction endpoint, distinct from the KM522 500 mM salt-protection experiment and from a direct catalytic salt effect. None of these whole-cell comparisons is attributed to the pACS31 inverted-membrane assay.

after.description: MC4100 reporter/loss-rescue context: active wild-type or pRM1-complemented SdaR/CdaR is inferred from loss in JA176 (paper-numbered P297S) and JA177 (Tn5 20 nt before stop); these mutants are not active endpoints. The paper uses a 391-aa reference versus current P37047 (385 aa); residue numbering is not mapped to the current chain.

evidence.source_assertion: The paper reports a 391-residue yaeG/sdaR reference, JA176 Pro297-to-Ser substitution and JA177 Tn5 insertion 20 nucleotides before the stop codon. These loss mutants inform regulator assignment.

pRM1 contains MC4100 sdaR amplified and cloned in pBluescript; it restores JA176/JA177 growth on glucarate, galactarate and glycerate. Loss and rescue support an activator role, not activation by mutant proteins.

MC4100 sdaR-promoter-lacZ reporters respond to the three inducing carbon sources only with functional SdaR. The source interprets loss of sdaR-lacZ and garP-lacZ activation in knockouts as positive control.
The current issuing P37047 reference is 385 residues; its gene name is cdaR with sdaR and yaeG synonyms. This anchors identity, not equivalence to the paper’s 391-residue sequence numbering.
